findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side limit ignores SiteSetting max image/attachment sizes
findings.body: The client-side upload validation previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] (i.e. max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb) but now hardcodes 10MB. This breaks validation in both directions: on sites where the admin set a lower limit (e.g. 4MB), oversized files pass the client check and only fail on the server with a confusing generic error; and the hardcoded 10MB cap cannot be raised by admins. The same hardcode in the 413 handler (line 246) shows users a wrong maximum size in the error message. The stated goal of the PR (allow large images that the server will downsize) is undermined because the client still blocks any image over 10MB and, worse, blocks images over the (possibly small) configured limit that the new server-side downsizing was meant to accept — the client check should be relaxed or removed for images, not fixed at 10MB.

findings.title: In-place downsize: convert is run with input and output as the same file path
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) executes ImageMagick's `convert /tmp/xxx /tmp/xxx`, i.e. the source and destination are the same path. ImageMagick reads the input lazily and can truncate/corrupt the file while writing, or fail outright, depending on format and buffering. The result can be a corrupted or zero-byte upload. The downsized output should be written to a separate temp file and then replace the original.

findings.title: Animated GIFs lose animation and animated path is never selected for uploads
findings.body: The animated-image branch in OptimizedImage.optimize is chosen only when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `tempfile.path` for an uploaded file is a Tempfile path with no .gif extension (e.g. /tmp/d discourse-upload...). So animated GIFs always go through `convert #{from}[0] ...`, which keeps only the first frame, silently destroying animation. Additionally, `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is passed, but the actual check inside optimize tests the file path's extension, not the flag, so the setting has no effect here. Files with no recognizable animation possible (corrupt images) will also make `convert` fail repeatedly (see next finding).

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failures and still submits the oversized file
findings.body: The while loop decrements `attempt` but never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, which returns false when convert fails (corrupt image, missing ImageMagick, etc.). On failure the file size never changes, so the loop pointlessly shells out 5 times and then passes the still-oversized file to Upload.create_for, which will reject it with a generic error. The loop should break out and fail fast (or surface a clear error) when downsize returns false.

findings.title: Duplicate definition of self.downsize; first (width/height) form is dead code
findings.body: The class now defines `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and then redefines `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby silently discards the first definition (with a 'method redefined' warning in some modes), and both have the same arity so callers passing width and height as separate integers will now hit the second definition and produce a broken dimension string like "640x480" vs "1024-768"-style concatenation issues... concretely, a caller invoking downsize(from, to, 100, 75) now gets dimensions "100" passed to ImageMagick (75 is bound to opts), producing wrong output rather than an error. The two-integer variant should be removed entirely or the definitions merged, not left as shadowed duplicate definitions.

findings.title: API URL download cap hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings
findings.body: FileHelper.download for API-provided URLs now uses a fixed 10.megabytes cap instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. On sites where max_image_size_kb (or max_attachment_size_kb) is configured above 10MB, valid API uploads are now truncated/fail at 10MB with no way to configure it; below 10MB, non-image downloads are no longer bounded by the image setting at all. The cap should be derived from the relevant setting (e.g. [max_image_size_kb, max_attachment_size_kb].max) rather than hardcoded.

findings.title: Downsized image keeps original filename but stored sha/filesize mismatch metadata assumptions
findings.body: After downsizing, the upload is created with the original `filename` and the new (smaller) tempfile.size, but the content no longer matches the file the user chose; more importantly, uploads of type where FileHelper.is_image? matches by extension (e.g. .svg) will run ImageMagick `convert` on an SVG with "80%" geometry, which either rasterizes the SVG (destroying its vector nature) or fails. SVGs should be excluded from the downsize path the same way OptimizedImage.create_for special-cases .svg.
